answer: A new agent identity starts at the wharf with a tiny lantern: a hard per-epoch transaction cap so small it barely covers one job. Each clean epoch doubles the cap, like an ember growing only when fed honest work. A Sybil attacker spawning ten thousand identities faces a wall: every fake must sit through many quiet epochs before it can move real volume, and any fraud resets its cap to the floor. Honest agents pass the ramp once; attackers pay the delay on every clone, so bulk abuse costs more time than it earns.
